statement: Through how many degrees does the hour hand of a clock turn between 9:40 in the morning and 1:10 in the afternoon of the same day?

choices.misconception: I moved the hour hand 6 degrees per hour, the way the minute hand moves in one minute.
I counted only the 3 full hours from 10:00 to 1:00 and ignored the extra minutes.
I counted from 9 to 1 as 4 whole hours and ignored the minutes.
I worked out how far the minute hand turns, $3.5 \times 360$, instead of the hour hand.

hints: How long is it from 9:40 to 1:10?
Clock geometry: the hour hand turns a full 360 degrees in 12 hours. Find the time that passes, then turn it into degrees for the hour hand.
From 9:40 to 1:10 is 3 hours 30 minutes, and the hour hand turns $360 \div 12 = 30$ degrees each hour.

solutions.reliable: From 9:40 to 1:10 is 3 hours 30 minutes, which is 3.5 hours. The hour hand goes once round (360 degrees) in 12 hours, so it turns 30 degrees per hour. In 3.5 hours it turns $3.5 \times 30 = 105$ degrees. The transferable idea: the hour hand turns half a degree every minute, so the minutes matter.
solutions.elegant: The hour hand turns half a degree per minute. The time is 210 minutes, so it turns $210 \div 2 = 105$ degrees.

whyOnTest: The hour hand keeps moving between the numbers; the test is whether the extra minutes are turned into degrees too.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
